name: Ramen Do
tagline: The broth simmers for eighteen hours, the noodles are made every morning
niche: Ramen bar and Japanese street food

listing.description: A site for a ramen bar, Asian café or late-night street food. A flickering neon sign, steam over the bowl and a menu laid out like a Japanese ticket machine.

seo.title: Ramen Do — ramen bar in Tashkent open till 2 am
seo.description: Tonkotsu, shoyu and miso ramen on an eighteen-hour broth, gyoza and takoyaki. Order at the ticket machine, open till 2:00 on weekends. Delivery across Tashkent.
seo.answer: Ramen Do is a ramen bar at 59A Mustaqillik St in Tashkent, open from 12:00 to midnight and till 2:00 on Fridays and weekends. Tonkotsu ramen costs 79,000 UZS, shoyu 72,000 UZS, miso 74,000 UZS and gyoza 39,000 UZS. Order at the ticket machine by the door; delivery is available.

sections.title: Ramen Do
sections.subtitle: The bone broth simmers for eighteen hours, noodles are pulled every morning and eggs marinate for a day. Grab a ticket at the machine and take a seat at the counter.

sections.label: The bar
sections.title: Eighteen counter seats and one stockpot
sections.text: Chef Timur trained under a master in Fukuoka and brought back one rule: a single broth taken all the way is better than ten average ones. The 120-litre pot sits right behind the counter — you can watch them skim it and pull the noodles. We talk loud and eat fast and hot.

sections.label: Menu
sections.title: Press a button, get a ticket

items.name: Tonkotsu
items.text: Creamy beef bone broth, chashu, egg, nori

items.name: Shoyu
items.text: Clear chicken broth seasoned with soy

items.name: Spicy tantanmen
items.text: Sesame paste, minced beef, chilli oil

items.name: Kaedama
items.text: A second portion of noodles for your broth

items.title: Ticket
items.text: Choose your ramen at the machine by the door, pay by card or cash.

items.title: Order sheet
items.text: Tick noodle firmness, richness and heat — from zero to five chillies.

items.title: Counter
items.text: Hand the ticket to the cook and watch your bowl come together. About seven minutes.

items.title: Kaedama
items.text: Broth left over? Press the button again and we add more noodles.

items.quote: The only place in town where at 1 am you get a proper hot broth instead of a shawarma.
items.author: Kamila

items.quote: The ticket machine threw me at first — now it is the best part of the night.
items.author: Jasur

items.quote: Four-chilli heat is honest. None of my friends has managed five yet.
items.author: Li Min

items.q: Is there pork in the ramen?
items.a: No. Our broths are made from beef bones and chicken, and the chashu is beef.
No bookings: the counter works first come, first served, and the wait is rarely over ten minutes.
Yes, a miso on mushroom broth with tofu — press the “Veg” button on the machine.
Noodles and broth travel separately in a thermal bag. You combine them at home in ten seconds.

sections.label: Contact
sections.title: Hungry at midnight?
sections.text: Walk in, no booking, or order delivery on Telegram — we bring it hot within 40 minutes.
